findings.title: DMARC policy is p=none
findings.detail: Monitoring only: spoofed mail is not blocked. Fine as step one, but plan the move to quarantine and reject once reports are clean.

findings.title: DMARC has no rua= reporting address
findings.detail: Without aggregate reports you cannot see who sends as your domain or what fails alignment.

fix.name: _dmarc.dmarc-none.example
fix.note: Same record plus a reporting address. Create the mailbox or swap in a report processor.

findings.title: No MTA-STS record
findings.detail: Optional but expected on a mature sending domain: it forces TLS for inbound mail and is what TLS-RPT reports on. Publish the TXT record and host the policy file over HTTPS (start in testing mode).

fix.name: _mta-sts.dmarc-none.example
fix.note:
Then serve this file at https://mta-sts.dmarc-none.example/.well-known/mta-sts.txt (a valid HTTPS certificate for mta-sts.dmarc-none.example is required):
version: STSv1
mode: testing
mx: aspmx.l.google.com
mx: alt1.aspmx.l.google.com
max_age: 86400

findings.title: No TLS-RPT record
findings.detail: TLS-RPT sends you daily reports about failed TLS deliveries to your domain. Pairs with MTA-STS.

fix.name: _smtp._tls.dmarc-none.example
fix.note: Create the tls-reports mailbox or point rua= at a report processor.

findings.title: No BIMI record (optional)
findings.detail: BIMI shows your logo in supporting inboxes. It needs DMARC at quarantine/reject with pct=100, an SVG Tiny PS logo and (for Gmail's checkmark) a VMC/CMC certificate. Not needed for deliverability.

cold_email_send_guidance.label: GUIDANCE (rules of thumb, not a DNS finding)
items: Send cold outreach from a separate subdomain or secondary domain (for example mail.dmarc-none.example), not your primary domain, so a reputation problem cannot hit your everyday mail.

Warm up new mailboxes: start with a handful of messages a day and raise volume gradually over 3-4 weeks. Keep daily volume per mailbox modest; there is no official number, so treat any figure as a rule of thumb.
Watch Google Postmaster Tools. Google's published guidance is to keep the user-reported spam rate under 0.30% (and ideally under 0.10%).
Add a working unsubscribe/opt-out to every campaign. Bulk marketing mail to Gmail and Yahoo needs one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058): check a real message with `email-auth-grader headers message.eml`.
Authenticate with the same domain you put in the From header (alignment) and verify DNS changes before launching a campaign.
Keep DMARC at p=none only while you collect reports; plan the move to quarantine.
Fix the high and medium findings above before sending any volume from this domain.

next_step.why: p=none without rua= gives you no reports, so you cannot tell what is safe to enforce.
